title: HUB (the base's middle: twelve facets round a sunken operations pit)
height: walls 3.1 m, roof rising 1.85 m to its apex hub
notes: Facets, apothem, walls' height, the pit's size and floor and the doors' bearings are the inventory's room layout (data/inventory/hub.json); the facets turned 15 degrees so a facet's middle faces each door's bearing. The roof's rise (1.85 m) and the doors' 2.2 x 2.6 m are the old record's (an unverified seed), not yet measured against the M3 views.

Bearings in the hub's own frame (0 north, -z; 90 east, +x). The hub's seat is turned half round on the Moon ground, so its bearing 0 faces the base's south (the lab), 90 its west (the greenhouse), 180 its north (the habitat), 270 its east (the workshop), 330 the airlock.
The concept is the M3 world's six views (the inventory's plan views v1 to v6); no single picture.

concept.read: the M3 world's six views (north, north-east, east, south, west, north-west) read element by element (scene-record stage, 2026-10-12), each element mapped to the inventory's rows (data/inventory/hub.json), or dropped with its reason

0.why: the tube hatch onto the lab tube (data/definitions/base.json lab_tube), which runs to the lab's north hatch

90.why: the tube hatch onto the west walkway tube seated on the Moon ground, which runs to the greenhouse's east hatch

180.why: the tube hatch onto the habitat tube (data/definitions/base.json habitat_tube), which runs to the habitat's south hatch

270.why: the tube hatch onto the east walkway tube (data/definitions/base.json east_tube), which runs to the workshop's west hatch

330.why: the hatch straight into the airlock's inner door (data/definitions/base.json airlock, its north wall against this facet)

elements.element: pressure hatches with hand wheels in the facets, one striped yellow and black (the airlock's)
tread mats and gratings before the hatches
the roof's lattice of ribs, diamond struts and node plates over ribbed panels to an apex hub
cable trays and a duct hung under the roof
strip lamps over the hatches, flood lamps under the roof, caged wall lamps
the sunken pit with its curved wall panels, floor plates, a stair down
the operations console of screens and keyboards round the pit, its chair
the railing round the pit's rim and down the stair
elements.drop: no row holds it: the inventory has no pit railing (a gap reported to the captain for the inventory and kit owners), not a reason to leave it out of the room

elements.element: a porthole in a wall panel
pipes with elbows and red hand-wheel valves on the walls
cable bundles along the walls' tops and drops down them, conduit boxes
tool board of hand tools
the big wall display and a cluster of small screens
notice board of pinned papers
comms desk with a radio, telephone, desk lamp and a headset on a hook
lab bench with a glovebox and a microscope
tall double locker and single steel lockers
low steel cupboards under the notice board and beside the display
elements.drop: no row holds them: the inventory has no low cupboard (a gap reported to the captain for the inventory and kit owners)

elements.element: door control boxes, readouts, an intercom and grab bars by the hatches
waste bin
worn, patched and vented wall panels with pipe and cable runs, posts, cornice and skirting
cracked deck plates round the pit, an access cover, a machine bay plate

far_ground.why: the hub's portholes look out on the Moon's ground to the horizon; reach and step the old record's (an unverified seed)
